questions.prompt: Should every discovery run begin with a mandatory deterministic local repository inventory, with dependency-cruiser, SCIP, or similar analyzers contributing only optional bounded observations?
questions.rationale: A stable minimum inventory prevents analyzer availability from changing the module contract while keeping specialized analysis replaceable.
options: Require a version-pinned native inventory adapter; treat specialized analyzers as optional contributors (recommended)
Require each selected external analyzer to provide the entire discovery result

questions.prompt: How should incomplete or low-confidence discovery affect progression to ArchitectureDesign?
questions.rationale: Treating uncertainty as certainty can create an incorrect baseline, while blocking on every minor unknown can make discovery unusable.
options: Block only on declared material gaps; preserve non-blocking low-confidence findings and require explicit Gate disposition (recommended)
Block ArchitectureDesign whenever any discovery finding is low-confidence or unknown

questions.prompt: What repository-access and privacy boundary should ArchitectureDiscovery use by default?
questions.rationale: Discovery may inspect proprietary source, generated output, ignored files, secrets, and dependency metadata, so its default boundary must be explicit.
options: Analyze tracked or explicitly declared files offline, respect ignore and secret rules, and require opt-in before source content leaves the host (recommended)
Allow configured analyzers to inspect or transmit any repository content allowed by their host credentials
